2_Introduction: The PSCs show a champion PCE of 25.2585% with VOC of 1.1832 V, JSC of 26.228 mA/cm² and FF of 81.3931%. The Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 (1.65 mol/L) perovskite precursor solution was prepared. The perovskite layer was deposited via a two-step spin-coating procedure with 1000 rpm for 5 s and 5500 rpm for 30 s. A total of 150 µL of CB was dripped onto the center of film at 15 s before the end of spin-coating. The substrates were sequentially heated at 110 °C for 15 min for perovskite crystal formation.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite film, based on a Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃ formulation with a relatively high precursor concentration (1.65 mol/L), benefits from the synergistic A-site cation mixture where FA⁺ ensures a narrow bandgap, Cs⁺ enhances thermal stability, and MA⁺ aids crystallization, collectively optimizing the tolerance factor and phase stability. The two-step spin-coating procedure, initiating at 1000 rpm for wetting followed by a rapid 5500 rpm stage coupled with a precisely timed chlorobenzene antisolvent drip at 15 seconds before the end, rapidly quenches the solution to induce a high density of uniform nucleation sites, while the subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 15 minutes facilitates complete conversion and controlled grain growth, minimizing pinholes and reducing the density of grain boundary and bulk defects. The enhanced film quality is corroborated by the pronounced increase in photoluminescence intensity and a slight red-shift in the peak position upon treatment, indicative of significantly suppressed non-radiative recombination and possible lattice relaxation, while X-ray diffraction analysis confirms improved crystallinity with a more intense and narrower (110) peak alongside the effective suppression of the residual PbI₂ phase at ~12.6°, jointly evidencing superior structural perfection and complete precursor conversion. This meticulous control over crystallization kinetics and defect suppression yielded a high-performance solar cell with a champion power conversion efficiency of 25.2585%, an open-circuit voltage of 1.1832 V, a short-circuit current density of 26.228 mA/cm², and a fill factor of 81.3931%.
